# Phase 6: Durable Execution & Idempotent Gate - Context

**Gathered:** 2026-10-12
**Status:** Ready for planning
**Mode:** Auto-generated by gsd-autonomous smart-discuss (auto-accepted)

<domain>
## Phase Boundary

This phase makes the **durable lifecycle** the real one: the demo and CLI execute the whole triage
run through `graph.build.checkpointed_graph` (the SQLite `checkpoints.db` saver), so a case paused at
the `approval_gate` survives a full process restart and resumes on a **stable, content-derived
`thread_id`**. It also fixes the idempotency-key breadth bug: the queue write must key on the
**immutable case input**, so an `edit` decision on resume **supersedes** the existing queue row
(updates its colour in place) instead of inserting a second row.

Delivers: AGENT-01. It **attaches at published seams** (a widened key in `store/queue.py`, a
derivation helper already in `graph/nodes.py`, a new `resume` CLI subcommand, a `--durable` demo mode)
and **edits neither the scorer, the citation helper, nor the audit interceptor** (D-18). It does not
add new scoring logic, new graph nodes, or new MCP tools — the graph topology is unchanged.

</domain>

<decisions>
## Implementation Decisions

### thread_id derivation & stability
- **D6-01:** Derive the `thread_id` from the **existing** `case_id_for(raw_note)` content hash
  (`core.hashing.hash_value`) — never a random uuid, never a per-entry-point prefix. The same case
  content therefore yields the same `thread_id` from any entry point and after a restart.
- **D6-02:** Hash input is the **raw note only**, through the one canonical hashing path — no second
  hash function and no ad-hoc string concatenation.
- **D6-03:** The derivation lives in exactly ONE place (`graph/nodes.py`, the existing `case_id_for`
  helper); the demo, the CLI and any durable runner **import** it. No caller re-derives or inlines a
  hash.

### Idempotency key breadth & edit-supersedes (the core bug)
- **D6-04:** The queue idempotency key becomes `case_id` + a hash over the **immutable case input**
  (the normalized `CaseInput` payload), NOT the scored outputs. An `approve` and an `edit` of the same
  case therefore re-derive the SAME key, so exactly one queue row exists per case.
- **D6-05:** The immutable-field set is **derived from the `CaseInput` schema** (DRY), not a
  hand-maintained tuple — a future case field is covered automatically and cannot drift from the
  schema.
- **D6-06:** An `edit` **supersedes in place**: the same key updates the existing row's mutable
  `colour` (and `target`), preserving `position` and `created_at`. No second row is inserted and the
  queue position does not move.
- **D6-07:** The v1.0 test that asserted "a different scored field produces a different key"
  (`RED != ORANGE`) is **rewritten** to assert the new contract: an edit supersedes (one row, updated
  colour, unchanged position). The old assertion is now wrong by design; the intent (one row per case)
  is preserved.

### Durable CLI / demo surface
- **D6-08:** `triagedesk demo --durable` swaps the in-memory saver for `checkpointed_graph` over
  `checkpoints.db`; the default (no flag) stays hermetic in-memory so the clean-clone demo needs no
  file state or model.
- **D6-09:** A new `triagedesk resume` subcommand drives the second half of the lifecycle:
  `resume --thread-id <id> --decision approve|edit|dismiss --approver NAME --role ROLE [--colour C]
  [--db PATH]`.
- **D6-10:** `checkpoints.db` lives at the repo root — the path already named ONCE in `graph/build.py`
  (`CHECKPOINTS_DB_PATH`) — overridable with `--db`; tests use a `tmp_path` file, never the repo copy.
- **D6-11:** On reaching the gate, `demo --durable` prints the derived `thread_id` and the exact
  `resume` command, then exits — a two-step storyboard whose second invocation proves the restart. It
  does NOT auto-resume in-process (that would not demonstrate persistence).

### Interrupt re-entry & exactly-once proof
- **D6-12:** "Exactly one audit record and one queue row" is proven by a test that runs the case
  through **two separate `checkpointed_graph` instances** over one temp checkpoint file (a real restart
  boundary), then asserts exactly one queue row and one `commit_priority` audit record.
- **D6-13:** The proof asserts the **audit count**, not the design's good intentions: `approval_gate`
  stays side-effect-free before `interrupt()` (D-04) and the checkpoint short-circuits
  already-completed nodes, so pre-gate tool calls are not replayed. No de-dup guard is added to the
  interceptor.
- **D6-14:** `--durable` resolves the real store seam (`store.default_store`) so the queue row
  survives the restart; tests inject the in-memory double or a tmp-file store.
- **D6-15:** Output stays **text only**; the `thread_id` is printed on one stable, greppable line. No
  `--json`.

### the agent's Discretion
- The exact `CaseInput` field list used for the key (read from the schema at runtime, not hard-coded).
- Whether the supersede is implemented as an `UPDATE` inside `upsert_queue_row` or as an explicit
  `read → mutate → write` in `commit_to_queue`; either is acceptable as long as `Store` stays the one
  seam and `position`/`created_at` are preserved.
- The precise text/format of the printed `thread_id` line and the resume-command hint.
- How the restart is staged in the test (two `asynccontextmanager` entries vs. two saver opens).

</decisions>

<code_context>
## Existing Code Insights

### Reusable Assets
- `graph/build.py` — `checkpointed_graph(tools, db_path=CHECKPOINTS_DB_PATH)`, `build_graph(tools,
  checkpointer)`, `run_case(...)`, `_allowed_msgpack_modules()`. The durable saver already exists; it
  is simply not the path the demo/CLI take.
- `graph/nodes.py` — `case_id_for(raw_note)` (the ONE content-hash derivation), `approval_gate`
  (side-effect-free before `interrupt()`), `_build_token(...)`, `_make_commit(...)`.
- `store/queue.py` — `commit_to_queue(...)`, `content_hash(...)`, `IMMUTABLE_FIELDS` (currently the
  scored outputs: `colour`, `target`, `triggered_rules`, `citations`, `used_vitals` — the bug).
- `store/__init__.py` — the narrow `Store` protocol (`read_queue_row`, `upsert_queue_row`,
  `next_position`, `read_queue_rows`, audit seam) and `default_store()`.
- `mcp/server.py` — `commit_priority` passes `content={"colour": committed_colour}`, which IS the
  key-breadth bug; the fix moves the key onto the case input.
- `evals/runner.py` — `_checkpointer()` (in-memory saver reusing the ONE msgpack allowlist),
  `_run_once(...)`, `_capture(...)`; `demo/run.py` mirrors this pattern for the storyboard.
- `cli.py` — argparse subcommands `eval` and `demo`; the place the `resume` subcommand attaches.

### Established Patterns
- Composition root: `build_graph` is the only wiring point; nodes depend on the injected `ToolMap`.
- Injectable store seam (`mcp.server.set_store`) so tests never launch the borrowed subprocess.
- One canonical hashing path (`core/hashing.hash_value`); one audit append helper
  (`store/audit.append`) wrapped by one interceptor (`mcp.server.audited`).
- Purity guards: `core/` never imports the model or an MCP client; `tests/test_purity.py`,
  `tests/test_no_duplicated_sats.py`.

### Integration Points
- `store/queue.py` `IMMUTABLE_FIELDS` + `content_hash` — the key-breadth fix.
- `mcp/server.py` `commit_priority` — pass the case input (not `colour`) as the keyed content.
- `cli.py` — register the new `resume` subcommand; `demo/run.py` — add `--durable`, derive `thread_id`
  via `case_id_for`, and use `checkpointed_graph` in durable mode.
- `tests/test_commit_idempotent.py` — rewrite the `RED != ORANGE` assertion to the supersede contract.

<specifics>
## Specific Ideas
- The headline is two properties, both provable: **"a paused case resumes after restart"** and
  **"an edit supersedes, never duplicates"**. Protect both above polish.
- The `thread_id` must be reproducible by hand from the note — a reviewer should be able to recompute
  it — so reuse the existing content hash rather than inventing a new identifier scheme.
- The demo's durable mode is a **two-command story** (pause → resume) because that is the only thing
  that actually demonstrates durability; a single command cannot.

</specifics>
